question: Should OpenClaw core adopt ordered read-only config layers as a supported Gateway CLI and lifecycle contract while the managed-configuration RFC is still open?
rationale: The implementation creates a durable public CLI/config mode with mutation, reload, hosting, and upgrade implications that code review cannot authorize from technical correctness alone.

options.title: Wait for RFC sponsorship
options.body: Keep this PR as a draft until the managed-configuration RFC confirms that ordered startup layers belong in OpenClaw core.

options.title: Sponsor and repair core support
options.body: Approve the core direction, then require the branch to reuse path-scoped write ownership and add coexistence coverage before merge.

options.title: Keep composition external
options.body: Have Lobster or another launcher compose and validate its inputs outside OpenClaw rather than adding a new core CLI contract.

recommendation.title: Wait for RFC sponsorship
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as a draft until the managed-configuration RFC confirms that ordered startup layers belong in OpenClaw core.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent configuration and Gateway stewardship makes this person the best available routing candidate for the core-versus-host ownership decision.
